Ragdoll-friendly clutter through the streets - benches, crates, barrels, market stalls and street lamps that fly when hit
Townspeople walking the streets, there to be launched around by a rocket or a sword swing

layout_placement.text: Spawn points set back from the open streets so nobody appears in front of a loaded rocket launcher
The ground the townspeople occupy and wander across

mechanics: Players spawn holding a rocket launcher and a sword
Ragdoll physics on people who are hit
Must be 3D, not 2D
notes: Battlegrounds preset taken for the free-for-all ragdoll brawl, but its flat bounded arena was swapped for a static settlement because the prompt asks for a town. Route is P0 either way.
physics-rig taken from Simulation - ragdoll props and breakable assemblies whose reactions are the entertainment is exactly what this prompt is about, and Action has no row for it.
Buildings treated as facades: nothing in the prompt says players go inside, so no P3.
Unclear whether the people being ragdolled are other players or town NPCs. Built with NPC townspeople present, since a town with nobody in it makes the ask hard to satisfy in single player.

handoff.theme: Modern Urban - an ordinary small town of shops and houses, paved streets, benches and street lamps

open_questions.ask: Who are you ragdolling - other players, town NPCs, or both?
How big is the town - a single square with a few buildings, or several streets of shops and houses?

captured: spawn holding a rocket launcher and a sword

preset_rejected.why: the prompt asks for a town, and bottomless ring-out edges around a settlement are the arena convention rather than anything the prompt points at

missing.ask: Who are you ragdolling - other players, town NPCs, or both?
Should the buildings be enterable, or solid facades you fight between?
Should rockets actually destroy the town - breakable walls, cars and props - or leave it intact?
What kind of town is it - a modern suburb, an old town square, or a city block?

enriched_invented.detail: a central square with streets branching out to shops and houses
ragdoll NPCs specifically as the targets
gentle elevation changes across otherwise flat terrain

notes_for_us: Ragdoll is the entire request and the only row that touches it is physics-rig, filed under Simulation as ramps and contraptions. A town whose point is that bodies fly around is not what that row was written for, and naming Simulation as a second genre for it feels like paying a classification cost to reach one option.
3D not 2D turns up in a lot of prompts and there is nowhere to put it. It is a constraint on the whole build and it ends in mechanics, where it means nothing to anyone.

A rocket launcher strongly implies destructible buildings, but the prompt never says so and step 0 warns against padding. The rule is right and the result is a town that will not break when the rocket lands.

unmatched_options.text: you spawn with a rocket launcher and a sword
make sure it is 3D not 2D
a town you can ragdoll in, and weapons to ragdoll people with

image_prompt.text: A tabletop-scale grid of even squares filling the centre of the diorama, where miniature figurines are positioned before the battle starts
The volcano tabletop board: rocky outcrops and glowing lava flows raised off the grid surface
Themed diorama surrounds framing the board - a desk cluttered with books, papers and stationery on one, a floating island of greenery and suspended platforms on another
Miniature collectible figurines - knights, mages and mech-warriors - standing on their grid squares at tabletop scale

mechanics: Casual strategy auto-battler
Collect, level up and customise mini-figurines - knights, mages, mech-warriors
Position units on the grid before the match starts
Once battle begins units fight automatically on programmed behaviours and synergies
Fast three-minute tactical battles against other players
Unlock board themes as progression
notes: Self-declared genre taken as written: casual strategy auto-battler is Strategy, and the board grid is its shape.
SET flag: nobody walks the diorama. The camera looks at it, units fight on it, and the whole thing is real geometry with no traversal to validate.

Three named board themes are three dressings of the same grid rather than three maps. Built as one board with the volcano theme as the primary dressing; if all three must exist as switchable sets that is a P4 conversation.
tile-grid rather than buildzone-grid: the same squares are both the board and the placement surface, and one entry avoids emitting the same geometry twice.

handoff.theme: Miniature tabletop diorama - painted figurines at model scale on themed boards: volcanic rock and lava, a cluttered desktop, a floating island

open_questions.ask: Should all three board themes be built now, or one to start with the others added later?
How big is the grid - what are the dimensions in squares?

captured: grid-based unit positioning before the match
three named board themes: volcano tabletop, cluttered desktop, floating island diorama

missing.ask: How big is the grid - 5 by 5, 8 by 8, or something else?
Is the grid split into two halves, one per player, or is it one shared board both sides deploy onto?
Should there be anything around the diorama - a room, a table it sits on, or nothing but empty background?
Does the board itself have terrain that affects the fight - lava that damages, cover, high ground - or is it a flat grid with the theme as decoration only?

enriched_invented.detail: a minimal or softly blurred background behind the diorama
the camera facing the grid directly or at a slight angle
visible unit placement spots marked on the grid

notes_for_us: Unlockable board themes are the second prompt in this batch to want one space in several dressings, and the vocabulary still cannot say it. Three themed versions of one grid is neither one map nor several separate ones.
Same collision as the other grid prompt in this batch: tile-grid and buildzone-grid both describe the squares, and nothing says which to take when the board and the placement surface are one object.
No grid dimensions were given and nothing in the handoff would carry them anyway except a count on the tile-grid pick, which is a strange home for the defining number of a tactics game.

unmatched_options.text: collectible mini-figurines - knights, mages, mech-warriors - positioned on the grid
unlockable board themes: volcano tabletop, desktop cluttered with books, floating island diorama
fast-paced 3-minute tactical battles

skill_gap.name: no theme variants of one space
skill_gap.why: an unlockable board skin is the same geometry dressed differently, and the handoff can only describe a single dressing
